**WHAT IS AN INPUT, AND WHAT IS NOT.** Of the folder this directive stands in, the ONLY files you read or snap are

operator's real `~/.claude*`.** In your chat messages name a compiled screen literal, never print it.

## Facts, measured by the overseer 2026-11-22T10:33Z — cite them as this directive's

- A bare `claude` on this host is 2.1.330, and THIS session runs it. The pinned product (the release build of
  `a59da9da`) holds none of the last seven mends and is untouched until its re-pin: it drives THIS session, so

- The tree at `66eb718c` holds 29 relied ledger rows, `MCP_CALL_DEADLINE` (55 s, its expiry `call-deadline`) and

- The entry, minted on the operator's own word (2026-11-22, «В Эпоху 4, после resize»): «the wrapper's paste into
  the child's PTY ends within a compiled bound; a paste that cannot finish ends the send with a closed word, the
  wheel unmoved». Its carries: the finding itself (one blocking `write_all` in `viola-pty`'s pump with no time
  bound; at the MCP call deadline the wrapper's `send` goes on and the driver reads `call-deadline`, the outcome
  unknown); `cry-m267ghbx`; the rehearsal red with its settle HYPOTHESIS, acted on only at its next red; the
  Epoch 4 boundary's advisory re-read (the operator's, at the boundary — not this chunk's work); a WATCH — seven
  rig rehearsals read red on verify's time-limited agents read in a light gate while a neighbour stalled the
  host on IO, green two minutes later on the identical tree.

     finding, said by name;

     largest paste viola sends;

     text in the input box with no Enter. Say what the next send, the human, and the confirmation then meet.
3. **The answer paths, each priced** (a non-blocking write with a deadline; a writer of its own with a bounded
   hand-off; a timed blocking write), with what each changes in `viola-pty`'s contract and who else calls it.
   For the recommended one say:

     under it, with the arithmetic shown); a new time bound is a named member of the a11y rows' lists;
   - the CLOSED WORD the driver reads at the bound — a new member of a closed detail or cause set is the
     operator's own (the exit-cause catalogue's rule); say which set, the exit code, and what the MCP result
     and the CLI's `send` print;
   - what «the wheel unmoved» means in code, and what is done about the cut text left in the box (nothing, said
     as a residual; a clearing key — a new typed byte class; a refusal of the next send until the box reads
     empty) — each priced, the choice a fork of the block;
   - what the human's keys do while a paste is blocked and after it is cut.
4. **Every master row whose words the change reaches: search ALL seven masters before the block is written**
   (`send`'s path, its time bound and total, the flight lock, the confirmation and «never presumed delivered»,
   the closed cause and detail sets, exit codes, the PTY pump's contract, the wheel, time bounds and who waits,

5. **At P3's END, before P4, stop with ONE block in `founder-forks.md`:** your window; what was measured with the

6. No live start and no rig start of a real `claude` in this chunk: a plan entry that makes one is a fork.
7. A new test child or a fake-agent behaviour (one that stops reading) is named, with the case that proves it

8. Every control stands on an entry filtered to its guard's own cases AND building the whole workspace where the

10. No mutation run. A test that waits takes a bound under the 20 s lint. Every TEST start runs under a test-owned

11. A fold is decided at the PHASE. A guard's or the permission classifier's refusal is never routed around: stop

12. Call NO scheduled-wake or timer tool, with any argument. End every process you start; remove no scratch

    refuses it.
13. Run the phase exactly as the letters say. On the P5 card, in one block, verbatim where a tool printed it: the

body: The measuring child is `stopchild.py`, kept with the harness in the chunk's `evidence/`. It answers `--version` with a non-claude line, so viola's start reads the CLI unverified and runs transport-only. It sets its terminal raw, draws one ready line, writes one tick a second, and never reads stdin until a control file appears. All of it ran under a test-owned user HOME, a test-owned viola home and a test-owned `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` (`target/pwb-xdg-{3,4,5}`: the scratchpad path is past `sun_path`'s 108 bytes, `local socket name length exceeds capacity` in run 2's detail line). It used the debug build at HEAD (`cargo build --features fake-agent`, 2026-11-22). Runs 4 and 5 read the same on every point below. Run 5 is `evidence/p3-stopchild-run5.json`.

- **The pty's capacity.** A raw slave that nobody reads takes 20 480 bytes from the master before a write would block (`evidence/pty_capacity.py`): 3 of 3 runs, and the same with a sleeping child holding the slave. A canonical slave never blocked up to the 8 MiB cap (2 of 2). The line discipline keeps taking bytes there, but claude runs raw. So a paste whose bracketed frame passes 20 480 bytes (a typed text past 20 467 bytes) blocks today against a raw child that stops reading. The largest paste viola sends is a typed text up to `MAX_FRAME` (16 MiB): `src/cmd/send.rs:57` reads `take(MAX_FRAME + 1)`, and the channel frame is held to `MAX_FRAME` (`crates/viola-channel/src/frame.rs:18`).

- **Where the bytes go and who blocks.** The wrapper's `send` runs on the channel server's connection thread. Under the send's flight guard (`src/run/send.rs:141-167`) it calls the attached closure, which is `PasteHandle::paste` (`src/cmd/run.rs:641`). That builds `ESC[200~` + text + `ESC[201~` + CR and does ONE `write_all` + `flush` while holding the shared input-writer lock (`crates/viola-pty/src/pump.rs:77-88`). The human's copy thread writes every chunk of stdin through the same lock (`HumanInput`, `pump.rs:92-108`). The output copy (`pump.rs:160-162`) and the resize poll (`pump_open`'s loop, `pump.rs:168-193`) touch neither lock.

- **What stops while it blocks** (send A: 200 000 bytes, child not reading for 39 s):
  - the driver's send: CLI `send` has no deadline of its own. It waited 47.0 s (47.083 / 47.029) and returned only after the child read again. It then ran its 10 s window and ended `not-delivered` / `no-prompt-submitted`, exit 13, because stopchild fires no hook. Over MCP, a block longer than about 55 s − the gate − the window reads `instance-unreachable` / `call-deadline` with the wrapper's send still running (inferred from `crates/viola-mcp/src/tools.rs:52` and the carry; not run here).
  - **a second send (finding 2):** send B (5 bytes, issued 2 s after A) did not refuse at once. It waited on the flight guard for the whole block, 35.1 s (35.081 / 35.040), then read `not-delivered` / `turn-running`. `decision/send-never-queued` says it is refused, never queued; today it is refused only after the blocked paste ends.
  - **the human's keys (finding 3):** a key `k` typed 3 s into the block moved the wheel to `human` / `human-input` at once (`events.ndjson`, 2/2). The classifier runs before the shared writer. The key byte itself was held behind the paste for about 33 s and reached the child after the paste's end marker and its CR (`k_bytes_after_paste_end: 1`, `k_bytes_before_paste_start: 0`, 2/2). The key is delayed "past the current atomic paste" exactly as `decision/human-keystrokes-never-blocked` allows, but that paste had no bound.
  - **hook events (finding 4):** `viola hook notification` returned in 4–7 ms (exit 0, nothing on stdout or stderr: `hook.event` is a notify). Its `activity` line was NOT in `events.ndjson` while the paste was blocked (2/2). It was appended only after the child read again: `append_hook_event` takes the same flight guard (`src/run/send/slot.rs:230-231`). A turn end, a prompt-submitted claim or a session edge arriving during a block waits the same way.
  - not stopped: the child's output kept reaching the outer terminal, 39 ticks in 39 s (2/2). No viola byte reached the outer terminal: no `unable` or `hint:` (2/2).

- **Recovery.** The wrapper recovers only when the child reads again. The paste then lands whole: one start marker, one end marker, 200 000 text bytes, CR right after the end marker (2/2). The held key follows, and the send runs its confirm window from then on. Nothing ends the block from viola's side.

- **What a CUT paste would leave** (a reading of the bytes, not measured on claude): the bytes already written stay in the child's input queue. A cut after the frame's first bytes leaves `ESC[200~` and part of the text with no `ESC[201~` and no CR: an unclosed bracketed paste. Every byte typed next, the human's keys included, would be read as paste content until an end marker arrives. A cut therefore has to close the bracket, and that closing write can itself block on a child that still does not read. The CR is never written on a cut, so nothing is submitted. The next send's readiness gate then meets a box holding text (on a verified CLI the gate reads the box only through compiled signatures, `decision/input-box-readiness-from-literals`). A pasted text would join the leftover in one prompt, so its confirmation would not match: `not-delivered` / `no-prompt-submitted` while a mixed prompt WAS submitted.

- `crates/viola-pty/src/pump.rs` (1-230, 704-874) — the pump's two copy threads, `PasteHandle` and `HumanInput` on one writer lock, the paste as one `write_all`, the pump's tests (`paste_*`, the `Rig`)

- `crates/viola-pty/src/lib.rs` (69-185, 612-625) — the `Pty` seam (`reader`/`writer` are portable-pty's `try_clone_reader`/`take_writer`), the hand-written `PtyError`, `CHILD_WITHIN` and its comment (carry cry-mui36h42)

- `src/run/send.rs` (1-330) — the refusal order, the flight guard around the second reads, the link, `send-issued` and the paste; a failed paste is `input-not-ready` with its cursor (`send.rs:168-171`)
- `src/run/send/slot.rs` (120-309) — `flight()`, `confirm`, `window()`, `append_hook_event` taking the flight guard, `Reserved`
- `src/cmd/run.rs` (620-680) — `pump_child`: the paste closure attached to the send slot, the pump started with the shared `PasteHandle`
- `src/run/gate.rs` (158-200) — `wait_ready` loops until a verdict; the feed queue `sync_channel(FEED_CAPACITY)`
- `crates/viola-agent-claude/src/screen.rs` (10-26) — `QUIET_PERIOD` 300 ms, `GATE_MAX_WAIT` 8.5 s, `CONFIRM_WINDOW_FALLBACK` 10 s, `COMPACT_CONFIRM_WINDOW` 40 s
- `crates/viola-mcp/src/tools.rs` (40-60, 655-680) — `MCP_CALL_DEADLINE` 55 s, `WAIT_CAP`, the arithmetic test `mcp_call_deadline_sits_between_the_wrapper_bounds_and_the_client_read`
- `src/cmd/hook.rs` (50-70, 571-600) — the spine hook's 750 ms connect budget, `hook.event` sent as a notify
- `src/cmd/send.rs` (50-60) — the CLI reads the text through `take(MAX_FRAME + 1)`
- `src/cmd/verify/typed/run.rs` (140-185) — verify's runs share the same `PasteHandle`; `paste_text` returns whether the paste wrote
- `src/bin/viola-fake-agent/input.rs` (full) — the fake agent's stdin parser; no option makes it stop reading
- `src/bin/viola-fake-agent.rs` (40-230) — its argv options (argv only, no env seam)
- `crates/viola-core/src/lib.rs` (260-285) — `NotDelivered`, the closed `not-delivered` details

- `~/.cargo/registry/src/…/portable-pty-0.9.0/src/unix.rs` (345-415) — `try_clone_reader` and `take_writer` are each `dup`s of the one master fd, so they share one open file description; `as_raw_fd` exists on the master, not on the writer

- **`PasteHandle::paste`** — 6 callers (trace `tree-query-2026-11-22-paste-write-bounded.json`, editor lines): `pump_child` @ `src/cmd/run.rs:641` (the attached closure; its call inside `send` at `src/run/send.rs:164` goes through the `dyn` closure, so the graph cannot see it), `Run::paste_text` @ `src/cmd/verify/typed/run.rs:182`, and four `pump.rs` tests (787, 839, 848, 872). A bound in `paste`'s contract reaches `viola run`, `viola revive`'s start (the same `pump_child`) and `viola verify`'s Run B, C and D pastes.

- **`pump_with_paste`** — `pump` @ `crates/viola-pty/src/pump.rs:122`, `pump_child` @ `src/cmd/run.rs:650`, `Run::spawn` @ `src/cmd/verify/typed/run.rs:152`, the tests' `rig` @ `pump.rs:747`, and the re-export @ `crates/viola-pty/src/lib.rs:16`.

- **A bounded hand-off that never blocks passthrough** (`src/run/gate.rs:190`): the vt100 feed is `sync_channel(FEED_CAPACITY)` plus `try_send`, and a full queue drops and poisons rather than blocking (`decision/vt100-feed-bounded-queue`). This is the nearest pattern for a writer of its own.

- **A failed paste after `send-issued` is `input-not-ready` with its cursor** (`src/run/send.rs:168-171`, `contract/send/paste-failure-after-issue`). This is the outcome a cut would take with no new word.

- **Worker threads under `catch_unwind`** (`pump.rs:30-40`, `spawn_worker`). A panic is sent to the pump loop, which kills the child (`decision/run-worker-panic-ends-run`). A writer thread of its own would be such a worker.

- **Time faked through injected seams** (`decision/time-faked-through-seams`). The pump's tests already drive it through injected readers and writers (`pump.rs` `Rig`, `Keys`, `Recorder`), so a bound passed as a parameter tests without a real wait.

- **`PtyError` stays hand-written with fixed messages**, no thiserror, the source boxed (`crates/viola-pty/src/lib.rs:69`; `decision/pty-error-hand-written`). viola-pty knows no agent and takes no Tokio (`decision/no-tokio-in-sync-crates`), so the bound is a parameter, never an agent constant inside the crate.

data.head: ### A. The writer of its own — `crates/viola-pty` (keeps arch S6; tests S1, S3, S4; obs S4, S5)

body:
1. **`crates/viola-pty/src/pump.rs`, the PTY writer thread.**
   - `pump_with_paste` hands the writer it takes from `pty.writer()` to ONE writer thread, started through
     `spawn_worker` and therefore inside `catch_unwind`. A panic there is `Worker::Panicked`: the pump kills the child,
     as for the two copy threads (`(obs-plan · decision/run-worker-panic-ends-run)`).
   - The thread owns the writer and takes write jobs from ONE bounded `std::sync::mpsc::sync_channel` in arrival
     order: a human chunk, or a paste.
   - The human's copy thread (`HumanInput`) sends each chunk it reads as a job and no longer takes a lock. When the
     queue is full it blocks on the send, so its next stdin read waits and keys stay in the terminal's own buffer.
   - Bytes are never dropped and never reordered.
   - The shared `Arc<Mutex<Input>>` writer lock goes; `NoInput` keeps its meaning: no paste before the pump opened the
     child's input or after it returned.
   - Sync and std only: no Tokio, no new dependency (`(security-plan · decision/no-tokio-in-sync-crates)`).

2. **`PasteHandle::paste(text, bound)`.**
   - It takes the bound as a parameter; viola-pty knows no agent (`(architecture · decision/pty-error-hand-written)`).
   - It builds the same bytes as today: `ESC[200~`, the text, `ESC[201~`, CR.
   - It enqueues them as ONE paste job, so no human byte interleaves inside it, and waits for the job's ack with
     `recv_timeout(bound)`, counted from the call.
   - The writer writes the start marker and then the text in chunks of at most 4096 bytes. Between chunks it reads
     the job's cut flag.
   - When every text byte and the end marker are written, the writer and the waiting paste make ONE atomic decision
     on the job's state (`Writing` → `Committed` by the writer, `Writing` → `Cut` by the paste at its bound; whichever
     wins). The CR is written only on `Committed`.
   - `paste` returns `Ok(())` once the job reached `Committed`, even if the 1-byte CR write is still pending: the
     send's confirm window then bounds what follows.
   - `paste` returns a NEW `PtyError::PasteCut` when its bound expired first. The writer then stops after the chunk it
     is writing, writes `ESC[201~` with no CR, acks nothing, and goes on with the queued jobs.
   - `PasteCut`'s `Display` is the fixed `"pty paste cut at its bound"`, with no source, beside the other hand-written
     messages (`crates/viola-pty/src/lib.rs:81-94`; keeps arch S6).
   - `Write(_)` keeps meaning a failed write.
   - Keep the `pty.paste_write` span as it is: `skip_all`, `text_bytes` and `paste_mode` only
     (`(obs-plan · contract/pty-seam-log/paste)` holds).

3. **What stays queued, and teardown** (`inputs#I2` item 7).
   - Against a child that never reads, the in-flight chunk, the closing marker and any human bytes behind them stay
     in the queue or blocked in the kernel write: at most one chunk + 6 bytes of the cut paste, then the keys.
   - The cut never waits on them: `paste` has already returned.
   - When the pump returns (the child exited and `pty.close()` ran, or a worker panicked and the child was killed),
     it drops the job sender and joins the writer thread. A write blocked on the closed PTY returns an error and the
     thread ends.
   - The join is bounded by the existing `KILL_WAIT` (2 s). Past it the pump returns anyway and leaves the thread
     detached, which the teardown case of step 5 reads red.

4. **`crates/viola-pty/src/lib.rs`.**
   - Add `PasteCut` to `PtyError`, with its `Display` arm and its `source` arm (`None`).
   - Reword the test-module comment over `CHILD_WITHIN` from «the nextest `mutants` profile's 10 s kill» to its
     15 s (5 s × 3). The 7 s bound itself stays (carry cry-mui36h42).

5. **viola-pty's own cases** (`pump.rs` tests, real threads, injected readers and writers as the `Rig` does; every
   wait bounded under 2 s; the bound passed as 200 ms; keeps tests S1, S3, S4).
   - A gated writer: a `Write` whose `write` blocks until its test releases it, then records the bytes.
   - `paste_bound_a_child_that_stops_reading_cuts_the_paste`: with the gated writer held, a 64 KiB paste returns
     `Err(PasteCut)` between 200 ms and 1 s.
   - `paste_bound_a_cut_paste_closes_the_bracket_without_enter`: after the cut the writer is released. The recorded
     bytes are the start marker, a strict prefix of the text ending on a chunk boundary, then `ESC[201~`, and no CR
     anywhere after the start marker.
   - `paste_bound_a_human_key_waits_behind_at_most_one_chunk`: a key sent through `HumanInput` while the paste is
     blocked is recorded after the closing marker and before any text byte past the cut's chunk. The case fails if
     the key waits out the whole 64 KiB text.
   - `paste_bound_a_paste_the_child_takes_is_written_whole_with_enter`: an ungated writer records start marker +
     text + end marker + CR, as one contiguous run (the existing `paste_is_one_contiguous_bracketed_write` moves to the
     new signature).
   - `pump_returns_with_the_writer_blocked_on_a_child_that_never_reads`: the child exits while the gated writer stays
     blocked, and the writer's `write` errors once the fake PTY is closed. `pump_with_paste` returns within 3 s, and
     the writer thread has ended (its join handle reports finished).
   - The existing `paste_*` cases (`pump.rs:787, 839, 848, 872`, editor lines from the code-graph query) take the new
     signature and keep their assertions.

    - Any other `Err` keeps today's `input-not-ready` with its cursor (`(architecture ·
      contract/send/paste-failure-after-issue)`).
    - `Ok` goes on to the confirmation as today.

12. **`src/run/send.rs`, the mark's rung.**
    - Right after the second human-typing and turn-running reads and before the link record, inside the flight
      guard, a set mark refuses `not-delivered` / `paste-cut` with no cursor: nothing linked, nothing issued, nothing
      typed.
    - The order becomes:
      1. `control-character`
      2. `empty-text`
      3. `human-typing`
      4. `turn-running`
      5. the gate (`input-not-ready`)
      6. `human-typing`, `turn-running` read again
      7. `paste-cut` (the mark)
      8. [link, `send-issued`, the paste]
      9. `paste-cut` (a cut, with its cursor) / `input-not-ready` (a failed paste)
      10. `no-prompt-submitted`

13. **`src/run/send/slot.rs`, the mark** (`inputs#I2` item 8).
    - `Flight` gains `cut_at: Option<u64>`, the human-key count read at the cut.
    - The rung of step 12 refuses only while `cut_at == Some(slot.wheel.keys())`. When the count has moved it clears
      the mark and goes on.
    - `append_hook_event` clears it (`None`), under the flight guard it already takes, for a `prompt-submitted` of any
      origin, a `session-start` and a `session-end`.
    - The mark is in memory only. It survives no wrapper restart, so a new `viola run` or a passed `viola revive`
      starts clear, and it is written to no snapshot.
    - It writes no line and no record of its own: its set shows as the cut's `send-refused` record, and its clears as
      the records that clear it (a `wheel` `human-input` move or a held key, `prompt-submitted`, `session-start`,
      `session-end`).

14. **`src/run/wheel.rs`.**
    - `Held` gains a `keys: u64` count that `human_key` increments (wrapping) under the lock it already takes, beside
      the typed mark.
    - Add `pub(crate) fn keys(&self) -> u64`.
    - A key that is no editing byte (the closed non-editing list) is not counted, as it moves no wheel
      (`(architecture · decision/wheel-classifier-only-observes)`).

15. **`src/cmd/run.rs` and `src/cmd/verify/typed/run.rs`.**
    - `pump_child`'s attached closure calls `typed.paste(text, PASTE_BOUND)` (`src/cmd/run.rs:641`).
    - verify's `Run::paste_text` calls `self.paste.paste(text, PASTE_BOUND)` (`src/cmd/verify/typed/run.rs:182`). A cut
      there reads `false`, as any failed paste does today. verify's pastes are compiled literals far under 20 480 bytes.

16. **The root's own cases** (`src/run/send.rs` tests through `test_support`, the clock injected; keeps tests S1, S3).
    - `send_cut_paste_is_refused_paste_cut_with_its_cursor_and_no_wheel_record`: a closure returning
      `Err(PasteCut)` gives `{"refusal":"not-delivered","detail":"paste-cut"}`, a `send-refused` record carrying the
      send's cursor, and no `wheel` line after the start offset.
    - `send_after_a_cut_is_refused_paste_cut_with_nothing_issued`: the next send after a cut is refused `paste-cut`
      with no cursor, no `send-issued` record and the closure not called.
    - `send_after_a_cut_clears_on_a_human_key_then_release`: after `human_key()` and a `release`, the next send passes
      the rung and the closure is called.
    - `send_after_a_cut_clears_on(#[case] kind)`: `prompt-submitted`, `session-start` and `session-end` appended
      through `append_hook_event` each clear the mark.
    - `send_a_failed_paste_is_still_input_not_ready_with_its_cursor`: a `Write` error keeps today's outcome.
    - The refusal-order rstest table gains the `paste-cut` rows, written as literals
      (`(test-plan · decision/send-refusal-order)`; keeps tests S3).

    - argv only, never an env seam (arch history n=23, `inputs#I2` item 9; arch S3 kept by adding no seam variable).

      list's own table).

18. **`tests/cli_send.rs`, one stamped home and a booted wrapper per case, the fake agent with `--stop-reading`.**
    Every wait is `WITHIN` (12 s) or under, below the 20 s lint. Each starts under a test-owned user home
    (`decision/run-under-test-owned-user-home`). The text is 65 536 bytes of `a`, past the 20 480 bytes a raw PTY takes
    (research).
    - `send_into_a_child_that_stops_reading_ends_paste_cut_within_the_bound`: `viola send --json` exits 13 with exactly
      `{"v":1,"refusal":"not-delivered","detail":"paste-cut"}` and stderr empty. Its elapsed time is at least 5 s and
      under `WITHIN`. The records after the case's own offset are `send-issued` then `send-refused` with
      `detail:"paste-cut"` and the same cursor, and no `wheel` record. The elapsed time goes to the evidence.
    - `send_after_a_paste_cut_is_refused_paste_cut_with_nothing_issued`: a second send after the first case's cut
      exits 13 `paste-cut`, its records hold one `send-refused` with no cursor and no `send-issued`, and its elapsed
      time is under the gate's 8.5 s.
    - `send_during_a_blocked_paste_is_refused_within_the_bound` (by-finding 1): a 5-byte send issued 1 s into the
      first send's block exits 13 within `PASTE_BOUND` + 2 s of its issue. Its detail is recorded as a READING, since
      it may honestly read `turn-running` (the first send still in flight) or `paste-cut` (the mark already set);
      either is a refusal with nothing typed. Measured today: 35.1 s.
    - `hook_event_during_a_blocked_paste_lands_within_the_bound` (by-finding 3): `viola hook notification`, fired 1 s
      into the block under the instance's `VIOLA_NAME` and `VIOLA_DIR`, exits 0. Its `activity` line stands in
      `events.ndjson` within `PASTE_BOUND` + 2 s of its firing. Today it waited for the child.
    - By-finding 2, the human's key, is held at the unit tier (step 5). A cross-process key case would need an outer
      PTY and a child that reads; that case's absence is stated here.

19. Run the whole unit, integration and e2e layers through the harness (entries 18–20). The WATCH (the seven
    verify-shaped rig rehearsals' agents-join red) is read from the integration layer's own lines, the host read
    first (entry 17):
    - a red with the host CONTENDED is recorded in the evidence and not re-run;
    - the same red on a QUIET host is a finding: stop and say so (`inputs#I2` item 10).

20. Write `.andromeda/cache/chunks/2026-11-22-paste-write-bounded/evidence/after-the-change.md`: the four
    cross-process cases' elapsed times and readings, against P3's 47.0 s, 35.1 s, about 33 s and «held until the
    child read».

- `crates/viola-pty/src/pump.rs` — the writer thread, `paste(text, bound)`, the cut, the teardown join, the cases of step 5
- `crates/viola-pty/src/lib.rs` — `PtyError::PasteCut`; the `CHILD_WITHIN` comment (carry cry-mui36h42)
- `crates/viola-agent-claude/src/screen.rs` — `PASTE_BOUND` and its value test
- `crates/viola-core/src/lib.rs` — `NotDelivered::PasteCut`
- `crates/viola-mcp/src/tools.rs` — the arithmetic test's paste term
- `src/human/hints.rs` — the `paste-cut` hint and its literal pin
- `src/human/mirror.rs` — the struck line's literal pin
- `src/run/send.rs` — the cut's refusal, the mark's rung, the cases of step 16
- `src/run/send/slot.rs` — `Flight::cut_at` and its clears in `append_hook_event`
- `src/run/wheel.rs` — the human-key count
- `src/cmd/run.rs` — the paste closure passes `PASTE_BOUND`
- `src/cmd/verify/typed/run.rs` — verify's paste passes `PASTE_BOUND`
- `src/bin/viola-fake-agent.rs` — the `--stop-reading` option
- `src/bin/viola-fake-agent/input.rs` — the stopped stdin loop

The block runs:

1. phase A: the formatter and the linter; viola-pty whole, then its four control entries, each filtered to its
   guard's own case;

2. phase B and C: the core, the agent crate and viola-mcp; the root binary's units, then the cut-mark control entry;
   the cross-process cases; the error-bodies census;
3. the host read, then the whole unit, integration and e2e layers through the harness;
4. the operator pass.
**What is not run, and why:**
- no round, no live entry and no live start (`inputs#I1` items 6, 30; `inputs#I2` item 12);
- no mutation run (`inputs#I1` item 10);
- no release-check entry (CI's `release` job runs it);
- `cargo deny check` is CI's `supply-chain` job (no dependency is added).

There is no boot-path touchpoint (no `src/main.rs`, no start order changed); the harness boot smoke runs in the
operator pass.

Every test start runs under a test-owned home, each case's own fresh directory, cleaned by its own teardown
(`inputs#I2` item 11). Every wait in a new case is bounded: 2 s at the unit tier, `WITHIN` (12 s) cross-process.

**The remove-the-guard controls** are implement's one-shot `gate.py control` runs, never entries. Each is fired on
its own filtered entry, which selects 0 tests on the untouched tree and its one case once it exists:
| id | File | The edit removes | Case | Fired on |

| `paste-bound` | `crates/viola-pty/src/pump.rs` | the bound on the ack wait: `recv_timeout(bound)` made a `recv()` | `paste_bound_a_child_that_stops_reading_cuts_the_paste` | entry 4, `--timeout 120` |

| `key-behind` | `crates/viola-pty/src/pump.rs` | the cut flag's read between chunks: the writer writes the whole text before it honours a cut | `paste_bound_a_human_key_waits_behind_at_most_one_chunk` | entry 5, `--timeout 120` |

| `cut-no-enter` | `crates/viola-pty/src/pump.rs` | the commit decision before the CR: the CR written on every path | `paste_bound_a_cut_paste_closes_the_bracket_without_enter` | entry 6, `--timeout 120` |

| `writer-join` | `crates/viola-pty/src/pump.rs` | the sender drop and the bounded join at the pump's return | `pump_returns_with_the_writer_blocked_on_a_child_that_never_reads` | entry 7, `--timeout 120` |
| `cut-mark` | `src/run/send.rs` | the mark's rung of step 12 | `send_after_a_cut_is_refused_paste_cut_with_nothing_issued` | entry 12, `--timeout 300` |
**Reading each control:**

- Each case's own waits are bounded (2 s), so with its guard removed the case fails on its assertion within its bound,
  never by the runner's kill. A `timeout` reading would NOT read the guard as held.
- `paste-bound` with `recv()`: the case's own 1 s bound on the paste thread's result fails.
- `writer-join`: the case reads the writer still running.

#!/usr/bin/python3 -I
"""Measures today's `viola run` + `send` against a child that stops reading its PTY.

Every path lives under one fresh run dir in the scratchpad: a test-owned user HOME, a test-owned
viola home, a test-owned XDG_RUNTIME_DIR. No claude is started. The child is stopchild.py.

Timeline (T0 = send A issued):
  A  a 200 000-byte send, `--json` (past the 20 480-byte raw pty capacity measured on this host)
  +2 s   B  a 5-byte send, `--json`
  +3 s   a human key `k` written to the outer terminal
  +4 s   `viola hook notification` (one activity event) under the instance's VIOLA_NAME / VIOLA_DIR
  +6 s   events.ndjson read: what stands while the paste is blocked
  +25 s  the child starts reading again (control file)
  then wait for A (to +60 s), read the child's report and events.ndjson, end every process.

Prints one JSON document of readings; the events are kinds, sources and data KEYS (never text).
"""
import fcntl
import json
import os
import signal
import struct
import subprocess
import sys
import termios
import threading
import time

REPO = os.path.abspath(os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)), *[".."] * 5))
VIOLA = f"{REPO}/target/debug/viola"
HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
CHILD = f"{HERE}/stopchild.py"
RUN = sys.argv[1]  # a fresh directory under the scratchpad, made by the caller
# The socket path must fit sun_path (108 bytes): the runtime dir alone sits at a short, fresh,
# test-owned path under the repository's ignored target/ (argv 2), never the host's own.
XDG = sys.argv[2]

os.makedirs(RUN, mode=0o700)
os.makedirs(XDG, mode=0o700)
HOME = f"{RUN}/home"
VH = f"{RUN}/vh"
for d in (HOME, VH):
    os.makedirs(d, mode=0o700)
CTL = f"{RUN}/release"
BIG = f"{RUN}/big.txt"
SMALL = f"{RUN}/small.txt"
with open(BIG, "w") as f:
    f.write("a" * 200_000)
with open(SMALL, "w") as f:
    f.write("hello")

ENV = {
    "HOME": HOME,
    "PATH": "/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin",
    "XDG_RUNTIME_DIR": XDG,
    "TERM": "xterm-256color",
    "LANG": "C.UTF-8",
}
INSTANCE = f"{VH}/instances/t1"
EVENTS = f"{INSTANCE}/events.ndjson"

t_start = time.monotonic()


def now() -> float:
    return round(time.monotonic() - t_start, 3)


readings: dict = {"marks": []}


def mark(what: str, **kw) -> None:
    readings["marks"].append({"t": now(), "what": what, **kw})


# --- the wrapper, under an outer pty -------------------------------------------------------
master, slave = os.openpty()
fcntl.ioctl(slave, termios.TIOCSWINSZ, struct.pack("HHHH", 40, 120, 0, 0))
run = subprocess.Popen(
    [VIOLA, "--home", VH, "run", "t1", "--", CHILD, "--ctl", CTL],
    stdin=slave, stdout=slave, stderr=slave, env=ENV, cwd=RUN, start_new_session=True,
)
os.close(slave)
outer = bytearray()
outer_lock = threading.Lock()


def drain() -> None:
    while True:
        try:
            b = os.read(master, 65536)
        except OSError:
            return
        if not b:
            return
        with outer_lock:
            outer.extend(b)


threading.Thread(target=drain, daemon=True).start()


def outer_has(needle: bytes) -> bool:
    with outer_lock:
        return needle in outer


def events() -> list:
    try:
        with open(EVENTS, "rb") as f:
            lines = f.read().splitlines()
    except FileNotFoundError:
        return []
    out = []
    for ln in lines:
        try:
            e = json.loads(ln)
        except ValueError:
            out.append({"torn": True})
            continue
        data = e.get("data") or {}
        out.append({
            "ts": e.get("ts"), "kind": e.get("kind"), "source": e.get("source"),
            "data": {k: (v if k in ("refusal", "detail", "holder", "cause", "confirmed") else type(v).__name__)
                     for k, v in data.items()},
        })
    return out


deadline = time.monotonic() + 20
while time.monotonic() < deadline and not (outer_has(b"stopchild ready") and os.path.exists(f"{INSTANCE}/snapshot.json")):
    time.sleep(0.1)
mark("child ready", ready=outer_has(b"stopchild ready"), snapshot=os.path.exists(f"{INSTANCE}/snapshot.json"),
     run_alive=run.poll() is None)
if run.poll() is not None:
    with outer_lock:
        print(json.dumps({"start_failed": run.poll(), "outer": outer[-3000:].decode(errors="replace")}, indent=1))
    sys.exit(3)
time.sleep(2.0)  # a quiet screen for the gate

# --- the sends -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
results: dict = {}


def send(label: str, path: str) -> None:
    t0 = now()
    p = subprocess.run([VIOLA, "--home", VH, "send", "t1", "--file", path, "--json"],
                       env=ENV, cwd=RUN, capture_output=True, timeout=120)
    results[label] = {"issued_t": t0, "returned_t": now(), "elapsed_s": round(now() - t0, 3),
                      "exit": p.returncode, "stdout": p.stdout.decode(errors="replace").strip(),
                      "stderr_bytes": len(p.stderr)}


ta = threading.Thread(target=send, args=("A_200000_bytes", BIG))
ta.start()
T0 = now()
mark("send A issued")
time.sleep(2.0)
tb = threading.Thread(target=send, args=("B_5_bytes", SMALL))
tb.start()
mark("send B issued")
time.sleep(1.0)
os.write(master, b"k")
mark("human key k written to the outer terminal")
time.sleep(1.0)
th0 = now()
hook = subprocess.run([VIOLA, "hook", "notification"],
                      input=b'{"hook_event_name":"Notification","session_id":"s","message":"m"}',
                      env={**ENV, "VIOLA_NAME": "t1", "VIOLA_DIR": INSTANCE}, cwd=RUN,
                      capture_output=True, timeout=30)
readings["hook"] = {"issued_t": th0, "elapsed_s": round(now() - th0, 3), "exit": hook.returncode,
                    "stdout_bytes": len(hook.stdout), "stderr_bytes": len(hook.stderr)}
mark("hook notification returned")
time.sleep(2.0)
readings["events_while_blocked"] = events()
mark("events read while blocked")
tb.join(timeout=30)
mark("B joined", alive=tb.is_alive())

while now() < T0 + 25:
    time.sleep(0.2)
readings["a_still_running_at_release"] = ta.is_alive()
readings["outer_dots_before_release"] = outer.count(b".")
with open(CTL, "w") as f:
    f.write("go")
mark("child released (reads again)")
ta.join(timeout=40)
mark("A joined", alive=ta.is_alive())
time.sleep(4.0)
try:
    with open(CTL + ".out") as f:
        readings["child_report"] = json.load(f)
except FileNotFoundError:
    readings["child_report"] = None
readings["events_final"] = events()
readings["sends"] = results
readings["outer_dots_total"] = outer.count(b".")
readings["outer_has_unable_or_hint"] = outer_has(b"unable") or outer_has(b"hint:")

# --- end every process this harness started ------------------------------------------------
os.write(master, b"\x03")
time.sleep(1.0)
for sig in (signal.SIGTERM, signal.SIGKILL):
    if run.poll() is None:
        try:
            os.killpg(run.pid, sig)
        except ProcessLookupError:
            pass
        time.sleep(2.0)
readings["run_exit"] = run.poll()
os.close(master)
print(json.dumps(readings, indent=1))

evidence/pty_capacity.py
body:
"""How many bytes a pty master takes before a write would block, the slave never read.

Two slave modes: raw (as an interactive TUI sets it) and the default canonical mode.
Each case writes 256-byte chunks to a non-blocking master until EAGAIN, then reports the total.
A second pass with a child process (`sleep`) holding the slave as stdin, raw, confirms the same
number with a real non-reading process on the other side.
"""
import errno
import os
import subprocess
import termios
import time
import tty


CAP = 8 * 1024 * 1024  # stop here: a canonical slave can accept without end


def fill(master: int) -> int:
    os.set_blocking(master, False)
    total = 0
    chunk = b"x" * 256
    stalls = 0
    while total < CAP:
        try:
            n = os.write(master, chunk)
            total += n
            stalls = 0
        except BlockingIOError:
            # The tty layer moves bytes from the flip buffer to the line discipline on a worker;
            # give it a moment and stop only after three consecutive refusals.
            stalls += 1
            if stalls >= 3:
                return total
            time.sleep(0.05)
        except OSError as e:
            if e.errno == errno.EAGAIN:
                stalls += 1
                if stalls >= 3:
                    return total
                time.sleep(0.05)
            else:
                raise
    return total  # reached CAP: never blocked


def case(raw: bool) -> int:
    master, slave = os.openpty()
    if raw:
        tty.setraw(slave)
    total = fill(master)
    os.close(master)
    os.close(slave)
    return total


def with_child() -> int:
    master, slave = os.openpty()
    tty.setraw(slave)
    child = subprocess.Popen(["sleep", "5"], stdin=slave, stdout=slave, stderr=slave)
    time.sleep(0.2)
    total = fill(master)
    child.kill()
    child.wait()
    os.close(master)
    os.close(slave)
    return total


for _ in range(3):
    print(f"raw slave, nobody reading: {case(True)} bytes", flush=True)
print(f"raw slave held by a sleeping child: {with_child()} bytes", flush=True)
for _ in range(2):
    n = case(False)
    print(f"canonical slave, nobody reading: {n} bytes{' (CAP reached, never blocked)' if n >= CAP else ''}", flush=True)
print("uname:", os.uname().release, flush=True)

#!/usr/bin/python3 -I
"""A wrapped child that stops reading its PTY: the measuring child of «Paste write bounded».

`--version` answers a non-claude version line, so viola's start reads the CLI unverified.
Otherwise: the terminal goes raw (as an interactive TUI sets it), one ready line is drawn, and
the child writes a tick to its output every 250 ms while it NEVER reads stdin, until the control
file `--ctl PATH` appears. Then it reads stdin for 3 s, writes what it read as counts (never the
bytes) to `PATH.out`, and keeps draining stdin until EOF.
"""
import json
import os
import sys
import time
import tty

PASTE_START = b"\x1b[200~"
PASTE_END = b"\x1b[201~"

if "--version" in sys.argv:
    print("stopchild 0.0.1")
    sys.exit(0)

ctl = None
args = sys.argv[1:]
for i, a in enumerate(args):
    if a == "--ctl" and i + 1 < len(args):
        ctl = args[i + 1]

tty.setraw(0)
os.write(1, b"stopchild ready\r\n")

started = time.monotonic()
while not (ctl and os.path.exists(ctl)):
    os.write(1, b".")
    time.sleep(1.0)  # 700 ms quiet between ticks: past the gate's 300 ms QUIET_PERIOD

released = time.monotonic()
os.set_blocking(0, False)
got = bytearray()
until = time.monotonic() + 3.0
while time.monotonic() < until:
    try:
        chunk = os.read(0, 65536)
        if not chunk:
            break
        got += chunk
    except BlockingIOError:
        time.sleep(0.02)

end = got.find(PASTE_END)
after = bytes(got[end + len(PASTE_END):]) if end >= 0 else b""
report = {
    "stopped_reading_for_s": round(released - started, 2),
    "bytes_read_after_release": len(got),
    "paste_starts": got.count(PASTE_START),
    "paste_ends": got.count(PASTE_END),
    "paste_text_bytes": (end - len(PASTE_START)) if end >= 0 and got.startswith(PASTE_START) else None,
    "enter_after_paste_end": after[:1] == b"\r",
    "k_bytes_after_paste_end": after.count(b"k"),
    "k_bytes_before_paste_start": bytes(got[: max(got.find(PASTE_START), 0)]).count(b"k"),
    "other_bytes_after_paste_end": len(after) - after.count(b"k") - after.count(b"\r"),
}
with open(ctl + ".out", "w") as f:
    json.dump(report, f)
os.write(1, b"\r\nstopchild drained\r\n")

os.set_blocking(0, True)
while True:
    try:
        if not os.read(0, 65536):
            break
    except OSError:
        break

body:
## 2026-11-22-paste-write-bounded — Design Philosophy: 1 row(s)
**Section:** Design Philosophy
**Change:** ~ decision/human-always-wins-wheel · rule: was «Human keystrokes are never blocked, refused or delayed past the current atomic paste; automation is refused with a typed reason instead of competing with the human.»; now «Human keystrokes are never blocked, refused or delayed past the current paste's in-flight chunk and closing marker; automation is refused with a typed reason instead of competing with the human.»
**Why:** decision/human-always-wins-wheel: The cascade's sweep of the retired mechanism found «the current atomic paste», false since the paste became chunks on one writer thread; the bound a key now waits is the in-flight chunk and the closing marker.
**Ref:** .andromeda/runs/2026-11-22T13-02-53Z-wrap/

- NEVER block, refuse or delay a human keystroke in `viola run`, or in a start a passed `viola revive` made, past the current paste's in-flight chunk and closing marker (the one exception: a start's automatic verify window, before any child exists, where a typed key waits in the terminal's own buffer until the child starts), and never count focus / mouse / resize sequences or terminal replies as editing (P4).

- cli: no interactive prompt, pager or redraw, and input is stdin / `--file` only; tui: once the child starts the terminal belongs to the child, and viola writes zero bytes of its own to it (only a start's automatic verify lines L1 to L5 and verify's own output precede the child's bytes) (under `viola revive --json` a `pump_child` error prints no document: viola writes nothing past it, and a peer the wrapper refuses is dropped in `accept_loop`, before its worker thread and any frame: it writes nothing to the outer terminal and moves no wheel), and once the wrapped child holds the terminal, human keystrokes are never blocked, refused or dropped: queued with the paste in arrival order, they wait behind at most its in-flight chunk and closing marker (the one exception is a start's automatic verify window, before the child starts: a key typed then waits in the terminal's own buffer), and focus / mouse / resize sequences and terminal replies (F-W2's closed list) are never counted as editing; every other byte is. viola has no web or graphical frontend; the terminal fleet console's keyboard reach is the route entry «Fleet a11y verification»'s.

- `validate_paste_text(&str) -> Result<(), NotDelivered>` checks decoded `char`s: LF/CR/TAB allowed; every other C0, DEL and C1 → `not-delivered` / `control-character`. Called by the CLI (and by `viola mcp`, which logs one client-side `send-refused` per refused `send` text) client side and again by the wrapper (authoritative). `RefusalReason` and the closed `not-delivered` details `NotDelivered` (seven values, `empty-text` an empty typed text on `send`, `paste-cut` the seventh: a paste cut at its bound or a standing cut mark) are kebab-case serde enums with `as_str`; `EventKind` carries the three `send-*` kinds.

- Wheel / dialog rules as in arch: `send` during a running turn → `turn-running` (a send's post-gate section — the human-typing and turn-running reads, the link record, `send-issued` and the paste — runs under one wrapper flight lock that the `hook.event` claim, turn start and end and wheel moves also take, a human key never; the turn lives in memory in `WheelSlot` beside holder and cause: `append_hook_event` marks it on a `prompt-submitted` of any origin and ends it on `turn-ended` / `session-start` / `session-end` before the line is appended; only a `release` that returns a human-held wheel clears it; a human prompt takes the wheel, so the send after it reads `human-typing` — except, on a verified CLI, an unsent human-filed prompt with no key typed since the last human-filed prompt and a scheduled wake counted at the last turn end: a fired wake, relabelled `harness`, the wheel kept); `pause` → `manual-pause`; a paste cut at its bound sets an in-memory mark at the wheel's human-key count, and while the count is unchanged the next send is refused `not-delivered` / `paste-cut` with no cursor, the mark cleared by a human key read, a `prompt-submitted` of any origin, a `session-start` or a `session-end`, and left by a key-less `release` or a `turn-ended`; only CLI `release` returns the wheel; a pending dialog is answered `null` at once when the wheel moves to the human.

- `RefusalReason` (kebab-case): `human-typing` · `unverified-cli` · `not-delivered` · `unknown` (`#[serde(other)]`; by design a code word outside the closed list stays visible in the document and in `refused: <word>`, and its exit is `unknown`'s 14 by `reason_of`). Details are closed per reason (`unknown`'s a code word or null, a code word being `viola_core::is_code_word`'s 1 to 64 bytes of `[a-z0-9-]`, a lower-case letter first); `reply_of` and `of_reply` read a `refusal` that is no code word as `unknown`, a string `detail` that is no code word as `null`, and a non-string `detail` as no known reply; `control-character` and then `empty-text` (an empty typed text on `send`) precede the documented order (`send`: human-typing → turn-running → input-not-ready → paste-cut of a standing cut mark → paste-cut of a paste cut at its bound → no-prompt-submitted, with human-typing and turn-running read a second time once the readiness gate's wait has returned ready, before anything is issued or typed, that post-gate section (the second reads, the link record, `send-issued` and the paste) running under the one wrapper flight lock the `hook.event` claim, turn start and end and wheel moves also take, a human key never taking it; `answer`: human-typing → unverified-cli → unknown-dialog). `unconfirmable` only ever appears inside an `ok` payload, as `confirmed: false` with detail `unconfirmable`: a ledger-listed local command whose post-condition is none or not yet measured, a stdout echo with no readable session transcript, a listed local command sent before its transcript exists, or any listed local command on an unverified CLI (never refused as `unverified-cli` on `send`).

- `validate_paste_text` allows LF/CR/TAB (multi-line relays are normal), rejects the rest — reject, never strip a refused character. Only allowed characters are rewritten or removed: after validation `send` types the text with every CR LF pair and every other CR as one LF and without its trailing CR and LF characters, and the delivery confirmation, the local-command list, `text_bytes` and the paste read that typed text (delivery is confirmed when the submitted text equals the typed text exactly, or is non-empty and equals it with its trailing run of ASCII space, TAB, CR and LF removed; no other difference, leading trimming included, is tolerated), which holds no CR (the founder's rulings, 2026-10-07T15:21Z for a trailing LF, 2026-10-09 for a trailing CR and CRLF, 2026-10-09T16:51Z for a CR or a CR LF inside). An empty typed text is refused `not-delivered` / `empty-text` (exit 13), by the client before any frame and by the wrapper before the first wheel read. A paste not finished within its compiled bound is cut: the bracket is closed with no Enter (no CR) and the send is refused `not-delivered` / `paste-cut` (exit 13).

- Before the FIRST frame of any method (including `hook.event`), verify the server: pid (+ sysinfo start time) against a `snapshot.json` that passed strict-modes in the same process (the socket-directory, pid, start-time and euid checks, none skipped). `viola hook`'s event and dialog paths run `check_instance` on the canonicalised instance (`canonical`, then `trusted`, in `src/cmd/hook.rs`) before the diagnostics level and obs init; a refused or absent instance exits 0 at once with no `config.json` read, no role file, no stdin read, no line, no frame and no SessionEnd append; the `--capture` arm stays ahead of the check. `verify` checks its home tree (`check_home_tree`: the home, `ledger/`, `bin/`, `plugin/`) before its `cli` log, and its `update_stamps` runs `strict::check_stamps` before it creates `ledger/` and again under its lock (a refusal `StampsError::StrictModes` reads and writes nothing, exit 1 with the home pair); `run`'s version gate reads the stamps through `read_stamps_strict` (a refusal is `cli_verified:false`). No dated strict-modes gap remains: every other frame client runs `check_instance` first, then reads the snapshot through `read_snapshot_or_replay` (a replayed or absent one gives no endpoint and so no frame), then the liveness-only pre-check, the socket-directory check on the recorded endpoint (`check_endpoint_dir`), the connect, the peer euid decision (`peer_admitted`) and the server check — CLI `send` (after its text read), `wait`, `last`, `answer`, `pause`, `release`, `link` and `unlink` through `client::refuse_untrusted`, then `live_endpoint` (the snapshot's pid + start time alive, the heartbeat live, an `endpoint` present; else exit 21, `viola_state::liveness::without_endpoint`'s `symlink_metadata`, which opens nothing and writes no line, reading `instance-dead` for an instance directory and `unwrapped-name` for an absent path or a regular file), then `client::connect` (the socket-directory check on the recorded endpoint, the connect, the peer euid decision and the peer pid and its start time against the snapshot's `pid` and `started_at`); `viola hook pre-tool-use|permission-request` past `trusted` writes its `hook.dialog` frame after its payload shape check through `src/cmd/hook.rs`'s shared `connect`; `viola mcp`'s `send` / `wait` / `last` / `answer` tools through the Tokio client after `check_instance` and `viola_state::liveness::live_endpoint` (else `instance-unreachable` with `detail` `without_endpoint`'s reading, `instance-dead` or `unwrapped-name`) then `check_endpoint_dir` (a refusal `socket-dir-refused`) and, after `TokioClient::connect`, the peer euid decision (a refusal `server-verify-failed`) and the server check. On a strict-modes refusal no frame and no line is written: the CLI frame verbs exit 21 with the instance `unable:` / `hint:` pair (under `--json` the `instance-unreachable` document, `detail` `strict-modes-failed`), `hook` exits 0 with no body, MCP returns `instance-unreachable` with `detail` `strict-modes-failed`. On a refused socket directory, before the connect, no frame is written: the CLI frame verbs exit 21 `instance-unreachable` (under `--json`, `detail` `socket-dir-refused`), MCP returns `instance-unreachable` with `detail` `socket-dir-refused` and writes no line, and `hook` fails open (exit 0, no body, one WARN `hook-decision` carrying `socket-dir-refused`). On a mismatch, a refused peer euid, or a check that cannot be made, no frame is written: the CLI frame verbs exit 21 `instance-unreachable` (under `--json`, `detail` `server-verify-failed`), MCP returns `instance-unreachable` with `detail` `server-verify-failed` and writes no line, and `hook` fails open (exit 0, no body, `hook-decision` carrying `server-verify-failed`); no line or output holds a pid, start time, path or endpoint.

- `validate_paste_text` over decoded `char`s: allow LF/CR/TAB, refuse every other C0, DEL and C1 with `not-delivered` / `control-character` — reject, never strip a refused character. After validation the wrapper's `send` types the text with every CR LF pair and every other CR as one LF and without its trailing CR and LF characters (`viola_agent_claude::hook::typed_text`; it holds no CR, only CR and LF are rewritten or removed, and no refused character is typed or removed), and the delivery confirmation, the local-command list, `text_bytes` and the paste read that typed text (delivery is confirmed when the submitted text equals the typed text exactly, or is non-empty and equals it with its trailing run of ASCII space, TAB, CR and LF removed; no other difference, leading trimming included, is tolerated); a paste not finished within its compiled bound is cut, the bracket closed with no CR, and the send refused `not-delivered` / `paste-cut` (exit 13). An empty typed text, the empty text included, is refused `not-delivered` / `empty-text` (exit 13) right after `control-character`: by the client before any frame and by the wrapper before the first wheel read.

- `.andromeda/obs-plan.md` §9 CI Integration, read whole by `rec.py render --section "CI Integration"` — the gates and their conditions (each fails closed; G2, G4 and the secret scan run even after a failed step; every artifact upload only when the job's secret scan succeeded, save the perf job's scan output, uploaded only when that scan fails), kept true in `ci.yml`

- **Fake agent:** `viola-fake-agent` (root `[[bin]]`, feature `fake-agent`) replays `fixtures/claude/<cli-version>/<Event>.<variant>.json` (the spine, the `<Event>.<stem>-<n>.json` dialog variants and the `paste-<n>` / `compact-<n>` / `clear-<n>` framing variants and the `SessionStart.resume-1.json` resume variant recorded by `viola verify`, the dialog tier by its Runs C and D, the framing tier by Run B's added pastes, the resume variant by Run E; `2.1.287`'s relayed dialog fixtures superseded and kept, `RELAYED.md`), runs absolute exec-form hooks from `<plugin-dir>/hooks/hooks.json` (every SessionStart hook child given each name of its set's recorded env names, always with the fixed value `fake-agent`) (and, under `--settings-hooks <file>`, a Claude settings file's hooks beside the plugin's, a command string with no args split on spaces and never run through a shell) (a group's `matcher` evaluated against a tool-bearing payload's `tool_name`), gates script steps on `--control`, and writes an ndjson `--receipt`; its cross-session sender resolves its target by the uds socket address alone, delivers only to its sibling and refuses an address not of the uds shape (its PreToolUse and PostToolUse hooks synthetic payloads naming the send tool), and its receiver reads its inbox only under the accept settings; its argv-only `--transcript` creates `<exe dir>/transcripts/` at 0700 at start and gives the launch SessionStart a `transcript_path` to a seeded 0600 file named by its session id (replayed framing variants not rewritten), and every stamping `viola verify` against it (harness `boot` and the stamped-home helpers) passes it `--transcript` beside `--framing` (the framing-free verify helper passes none), and every test-started `viola verify`, `viola run` and `viola revive` and every harness boot stamping runs under a test-owned user home whose config file is seeded empty and owner-only, never the runner's real `HOME` (the harness's supervised wrappers of a stamped session too, under a session user home seeded with an empty config), the fake agent told that config file by `--trust-config`, and every stamping `viola verify` of a test or the harness given a short owner-only runtime dir (`XDG_RUNTIME_DIR`) it owns for the stamp's life (the rig rehearsal sets its own only where the host sets none) (a `--record` verify keeps the real `HOME` and points a kept `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` at the test-owned user home instead); its print mode `-p/--print <prompt>` fires the spine fixtures, prints `ok` and exits 0, `--trust-config <file>` reads trust from that config file by the CLI's walk (the canonical cwd's exact key then each parent up to the git root, so inside a repository the cwd's own record counts, through a bounded read; any failure reads untrusted), `--screens` / `--trusted-root` / `--turn-stop` write `Screen.modal|ready|turn` (under `--screens` with an untrusted cwd it draws claude 2.1.325's unnumbered trust form over the set's recorded modal, the selector first on No; arrows move the selector, Enter on No exits 1, and SessionStart fires only after Enter on the trust row, which draws the ready screen), the argv-only `--stop-reading` makes it never read stdin, parked forever with its terminal left raw, so a paste into it blocks, `--turn-fail <variant>`, beside `--turn-stop`, ends the turn with the recorded set's `StopFailure.<variant>` payload in place of `Stop.default`, `--dialogs` replays a pasted dialog prompt's recorded variants in claim order, and `--framing` replays Run B's recorded paste, `/compact` and `/clear` variants (the probed `/compact` its recorded `SessionStart.compact-1` with the last fired SessionStart's `session_id`; the exact verify echo probe command or the exact `/context` probe command, like a stdout-tag local command under `--local-command-mode`, one stdout tag line appended to the last started session's transcript and no hook fired) for verify's six interactive runs (two capped test-only holds: `--stop-receipt-hold-ms`, 1 s, holds the Stop receipt for a race test; `--paste-hint-ms`, 10 s, holds a cleared screen after the long paste's turn; the test-only hold `--trust-record-blank` makes a start trusted by the trust record alone draw no screen, holding verify's Run F window open for a stop case; The committed `fixtures/claude/*/*.json` (the recorded sets, each with its dialog, framing and resume variants and its agents fixture `Agents.recorded-1.json`, Run B's own row of its one `claude agents --json` read, where it holds them, and 2.1.287's superseded relayed fixtures included; The panic hook writes one line to the role file (no stderr, never the default hook); `catch_unwind` at the main-thread catch site, around `hook` dispatch, the three `run` PTY threads (the two pump copy threads and the paste writer thread) (the child's exit is polled inline on run's main thread, under main's catch site), and the vt100 feed.

- Run start's span chain is `run.start` (INTERNAL, root) › `state.snapshot_recover` › `run.collision_check` › `run.pin_copy` › `run.version_gate` › `channel.bind` › `state.snapshot_write` › `state.heartbeat_start` › `pty.spawn` (CLIENT), with no budget span. The implicit link record on a `send` or an `answer`, the explicit `link` / `unlink` methods the driven wrapper serves (their trace the call's `channel-request` / `channel-response` pair, which holds neither name), the link set's restore at start and the replay's link rule carry no span and no process-log line of their own; `driver`, `driven` and `since` reach no home-level line. The wrapper's stdin typed mark and its held scheduled-wakes count are in-memory state that open no span and write no line of their own, and carry no key and no prompt text. The cut mark a cut paste leaves is in-memory wrapper state too: it opens no span and writes no line of its own, its set showing as the cut send's `send-refused` `paste-cut` record and its clears as their own `prompt-submitted`, `session-start` and `session-end` records. The send's transcript echo read (the end offset before the paste and the tag count after it) opens no span and writes no line or span field of its own; its result shows only as the `send-confirmed` line inside `run.confirm_window`. A `send-refused` line carries `refusal`, `detail`, `side` and `wheel`, never `window`, `used_percentage`, `resets_at` or `paused`. At a dialog hold's end (`run.dialog_await`'s `deadline_ms`, `config.json`'s `dialog_hold_s` in ms, 60 000–3 600 000, default 60 000) the wrapper appends one `dialog-expired{dialog_id, dialog_kind}` product line and writes one `dialog-answered{corr:<dialog_id>, dialog_kind, deadline_hit:true, duration_ms}` with no `from` / `from_trust`; a hand-back or an answer writes neither; the hook then writes `hook-decision{decision_emitted:false, deadline_hit:false}`, `deadline_hit:true` only when its own read times out at its backstop bound `DIALOG_HOLD_MAX + 5 s` (3605 s).
